title: The store survives an ungraceful process kill without corruption
asA: operator whose hosts die and whose containers get OOM-killed at unhelpful moments
iWant: the store to open cleanly on the next boot after an ungraceful termination, with every committed write intact and every in-flight transaction rolled back
soThat: a SIGKILL, a power loss, or an OOM event does not turn into a data-recovery incident

acceptanceCriteria.description: A write committed before the process is SIGKILL'd is present when a fresh process opens the same store artifact afterward.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running process that commits a distinguishable write W through a facade verb and then receives SIGKILL
acceptanceCriteria.when: a fresh process opens the same store artifact and reads through the facade
acceptanceCriteria.then: the read returns W with the same values that were committed, and the store event log's opened event for the fresh process is present with no accompanying corruption error

acceptanceCriteria.description: An in-flight transaction that had not committed at the moment of SIGKILL is not visible after the fresh open.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running process that opens a transaction, executes writes W_a, and receives SIGKILL before commit
acceptanceCriteria.when: a fresh process opens the same store artifact and reads through the facade
acceptanceCriteria.then: the reads for W_a's affected rows return the pre-transaction state and no post-transaction state, and no partial subset of W_a is visible

acceptanceCriteria.description: The store's durability posture (write-ahead log and synchronous commit floor, or engine-native equivalent) is set at open time by the facade; no consumer configures it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the store has been opened by the facade
acceptanceCriteria.when: the durability posture is inspected via an engine-native introspection query executed through the facade
acceptanceCriteria.then: the returned posture matches the facade's declared crash-safety configuration, and a grep of consumer code finds no direct configuration of these pragmas or engine-native equivalents
